Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ava (Cobalt Head of Platform), Diego (ML Eng), Lina (CTO)

00:00 Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, I'm the AE on the account, with Maya who's our solutions engineer.
00:06 Ava (Cobalt): hi, thanks, ava here, i'm the head of platform at cobalt, nice to meet you.
00:10 Diego (Cobalt): diego here, ml engineer, we'll be doing the initial prototyping.
00:14 Maya (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda - 1) your use cases and success criteria, 2) quickstart experience + free credits + time-to-first-token, 3) which deployment mode makes sense (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 4) security questions, and 5) next steps. sound good?
00:23 Lina (Cobalt): yes that works.

00:30 Ava: high level - we're building an ML-enhanced search and assistant inside our portfolio operations platform. want to prototype with embeddings and chat generation; low friction for PMs and data scientists to try. main asks: quick to get started, minimal infra, and then a path to scale to dedicated capacity if latency or cost becomes an issue.
00:48 Samir: perfect. so PLG quickstart is exactly for that - self-serve signup, free credits for devs, and our SDK/REST quickstart usually gets people to first token in under 10 minutes. Maya, want to add details?
00:58 Maya: yeah, for most teams we have a 3-step quickstart: create an org, redeem dev credits, get an API key, then run either the python SDK sample or a curl POST against the /v1/generate endpoint. streaming is supported out-of-the-box, and we ship example repo for embeddings demo too. common gotcha is firewall egress for corp networks but otherwise it's very fast.
01:18 Diego: how are free credits provisioned? like per-user or per-org? any limits?
01:22 Samir: good question - we grant an org-level credit pool for PLG trials; typical is $500-$2k depending on lead source. credits show up immediately, and we can set rate limits. for larger POCs we can extend with AE approval.
01:36 Ava: and time-to-first-token in practice? we have pentesting windows and a couple of internal approval steps - want to track realistic times.
01:42 Maya: most folks get token in under 10 minutes if they can paste a quick cURL; with SSO onboarding it adds time but the dev loop is very quick. we also have a browser quickstart that walks non-devs through generating an API key locally.
01:55 Lina: what about dev experience for embeddings? our data scientists use python notebooks.
01:59 Maya: embeddings are literally a single SDK call - client.embeddings.create(...). samples in our repo include notebook examples that run in a minute or two. we also provide similarity search examples.
02:12 Diego: when would we hit a point where hosted is no longer sufficient? we expect production to have spikes of concurrent users and long contexts up to 4k tokens.
02:20 Maya: depends on traffic and latency SLOs. hosted is great for low to medium volume and prototyping; for predictable throughput and isolation, Dedicated (reserved capacity) gives you pinned GPU pools and guaranteed QPS. Private is for when you need VPC/on-prem and strict data residency.
02:36 Samir: cost tradeoffs - hosted is usage-based so good for early stuff; Dedicated is commit-based and reduces per-token cost at scale. we can model typical cost if you share query distribution.
02:47 Ava: security - we need SOC2, SAML/SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. also data retention policies.
02:55 Maya: we are SOC2 Type II, we support SAML SSO via SSO admin settings, RBAC on project level, and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. for hosted we offer encryption at rest with our keys; we can also provide SOC2 docs and a security slide deck after the call.
03:12 Lina: any compliance concerns for european data residency?
03:15 Samir: we have regions in NA and EU; for strict residency you'd likely look at Private or Dedicated in-region depending on controls. we'll share the infrastructure region matrix.
03:25 Diego: technical - how do we run a quick benchmark? we'd like to compare latency and cost for 2-4k token gen on hosted and then sim a dedicated run.
03:33 Maya: we can spin up a short benchmark: 1) you give us 10 representative prompts, 2) we run 100 requests per prompt in the hosted env and capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost, 3) extrapolate for Dedicated. I'll run this in our sandbox org and share results.
03:47 Ava: that sounds good. how about the SDKs? we use python and node.
03:51 Samir: we have both, official SDKs and language-agnostic REST. sample snippets: python pip install redwood-sdk; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...). then client.responses.create(...). we'll include quickstart repo link.
04:02 Diego: any rate limits that will bite during prototyping?
04:05 Maya: default free-tier orgs have soft rate limits to protect fairness; we can raise them for your trial if you need. Dedicated lets you set autoscale and burst policies.
04:15 Lina: what's the path to Dedicated? do we need to sign an agreement?
04:18 Samir: typically once usage hits a threshold or you want contractual SLAs, we move to reserved capacity with an MSA. but you can prototype fully on hosted and then we migrate models and config; the API surface remains the same so minimal changes.
04:31 Ava: demo / POC timeline - we want to have devs try quickstart this week and then a benchmark next week, decision in ~4 weeks. is that realistic?
04:39 Samir: yes, that's the usual cadence. I'll send the quickstart + credits today and Maya will schedule the benchmark.
04:44 Diego: small nit - sometimes auto-generated transcripts mess up product names; is \"Redwood Dedicated\" spelled differently?
04:48 Maya: haha no, that's the name, but transcriptions often do weird stuff.

04:52 Samir: ok, security docs - we'll send SOC2 and SAML setup guide. Maya will copy the SE owner for the benchmark.
05:00 Ava: any blockers from our side? we'll need internal approval to redeem credits and temporary API keys - i'll own that.
05:06 Samir: perfect. recap and next steps: 1) Samir send quickstart + credits link, 2) Maya schedule benchmark and run in sandbox, 3) Ava share compliance contact, 4) follow-up call after benchmark.
05:20 Lina: thanks everyone.
05:22 Samir: thanks all, talk soon.

Notes / imperfections: some words mis-transcribed (SSO sometimes \"s s o\"), small crosstalk at 01:42, product name sometimes shown as \"Redwood Dedicatd\" in auto transcript.
